# Data Capture Tool - full documentation (generated by scripts/build_llms_full.py)

Local Flask + plain-JS app that captures one clean training image per vehicle from live RTSP streams inside
user-drawn ROIs. This file concatenates: README.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/API.md, AGENTS.md. Source files: backend/ (Python), frontend/ (static UI).


==============================================================================
# FILE: README.md
==============================================================================

# Data Capture Tool

Captures **one clean image per vehicle** from live RTSP camera streams, only while the vehicle is inside an area
you draw (an ROI), to build training data for detection models. Everything is local: no database, no cloud.

- **Any YOLO model** - your own trained weights (e.g. 7 vehicle classes) or stock COCO models (`yolov8s.pt`).
- **One image per vehicle, no duplicates** - tracking + duplicate suppression; the next car in the same lane is still captured.
- **Multiple ROIs per camera**, multiple cameras, **multi-GPU** support.
- **Browser UI**: live view with the newest captures beside it, ROI editor, camera manager, gallery, settings.
- **Plain files**: cameras in `data/cameras.json`, images in `captures/`, settings in `config.ini`.

> Using an AI assistant on this repo? Start with [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) and [`llms.txt`](llms.txt).

---

## Quick start

```bash
cd Data_capture_tool
pip install -r requirements.txt
python backend/app.py            # or double-click start.bat
```

The service listens on all network interfaces (`HOST = 0.0.0.0`) on the port set in `config.ini` (default **5100**).
It does **not** open a browser. At start it prints the addresses to use:

```
Data Capture Tool listening on 0.0.0.0:5100
  this machine : http://127.0.0.1:5100
  other machines: http://<this-pc-ip>:5100
```

Open one of those in a browser (other machines use the second address; allow the port in the firewall). Then:

1. **Cameras** tab - add a name and RTSP URL (`rtsp://user:pass@host:554/stream`), press **Test**.
2. **ROI** tab - choose the camera, **Load snapshot**, click to place polygon points (drag to adjust).
   Use **+ New ROI** to draw more areas on the same camera. **Save ROIs**.
3. **Settings** tab - pick the model, device, classes and thresholds, then **Save & restart**.
4. **Live** tab - press **Start** on a camera (or **Start all**). Captured vehicles appear in **Recent captures** on the right.
   Cameras that cannot start (e.g. no ROI yet) are reported by name and do not stop the others.
5. **Gallery** tab - browse, filter, enlarge and delete everything captured.

**Theme:** dark by default (neutral grey, same palette as the VIDES frontend); the sun/moon button in the header
switches to a light theme and remembers your choice.

Requirements: Python 3.10+ (developed on 3.11/3.13), Windows or Linux. A GPU is optional (CPU works, slower).

---

## The tabs

| Tab | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Live** | Settings summary; a camera toolbar with **Start all / Stop all** and a **Layout** selector (Auto, or 1-4 cameras per row, remembered); one live card per camera (video with ROI and detection boxes, status, counters, **full-screen** button, Start/Stop); and a **Recent captures** panel (the latest 10) with thumbnails + class tags. Click a thumbnail to enlarge or delete. |
| **ROI** | Draw one or more polygons per camera on a fresh snapshot. A vehicle is captured when it is inside **any** ROI. |
| **Cameras** | Add / enable / test / delete cameras. Passwords are masked in the UI. |
| **Gallery** | Browse all captures with camera / date / class filters and paging. |
| **Settings** | All model and capture options, grouped in sections. Nothing applies until you press **Save & restart**. |

### Settings (and what Save & restart does)

Edits collect in a draft - rows you changed are highlighted, sections show a dot, the top bar shows
"N unsaved changes". **Save & restart** sends everything in one request; any running camera is restarted
**once** with the new settings. Saved images stay on disk and the saved/skipped counters keep counting.
**Discard** returns every control to the saved values.

| Section | Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Model & device | Detection model | Any `*.pt` in `MODELS_DIR`. Switching resets classes to that model's defaults. |
| | Compute device | `auto` (all GPUs, else CPU), `cpu`, `cuda:0`, or a list `cuda:0,cuda:1`. Cameras are spread round-robin over GPUs. |
| Detection | Confidence threshold | Ignore detections below this score (0.01 - 1). |
| | Classes to capture | Searchable picker; "Vehicles" = the model's default set. |
| Capture | Image to save | **Full frame** (default), **Crop**, or **Both**. |
| | Capture moment | **Best frame (buffered)** (default): the best view of each vehicle is held in a buffer, a better frame replaces the older one, and it is saved once when the vehicle leaves the ROI. **First frame (instant)** saves immediately (lower quality, more duplicates). |
| | Keep metadata | Off (default) = images only. On = a `.json` next to each image. |
| Advanced | Minimum vehicle size | Shorter side in px (default 40). |
| | Minimum overlap with ROI | 0 - 1 (default 0.5). Stops half-in vehicles being saved. |
| | Duplicate window | Seconds (default 2). If the tracker loses a vehicle and gives it a new ID, a track that appears where it was expected within this time is the **same** vehicle. |
| | Maximum wait | Seconds (default 10). A vehicle that stays in the ROI (stopped / traffic) is saved after this long. |
| | JPEG quality | 1 - 100 (default 95). |
| | Detection size | Model input size in px (default 640). |

---

## How capture works

Per camera, three threads run:

1. **Reader** - reads the RTSP stream (TCP) as fast as it arrives and keeps only the **newest frame**, so slow
   inference never makes the picture lag. Reconnects automatically; open/read timeouts are 5 s.
2. **Detect + track** - runs YOLO with ByteTrack (settings in `backend/trackers/bytetrack_vehicle.yaml`, class-agnostic
   NMS) on the ROI area plus a 30% margin, so a vehicle half outside the ROI is seen whole.
3. **Saver** - writes files from a queue so a slow disk never drops frames.

Each camera loads **its own model instance** (ByteTrack state is per instance) on its assigned device.

### One capture per *vehicle* (not per tracker ID)

A tracker gives a vehicle an ID, but IDs switch (a missed detection, occlusion, a fast vehicle at a low frame
rate) and then one vehicle looks like two. The capture logic (`backend/capture_logic.py`) therefore keeps its own
notion of a **vehicle**:

- **Same object boxed twice** in one frame (e.g. 46x40 and 53x65 on the same car, or as "car" and "truck") is
  one vehicle: the weaker box is dropped.
- **A new tracker ID that appears where a just-lost vehicle was expected** (its last position + its speed, with a
  tolerance that grows over the *duplicate window*) is the **same vehicle**. A vehicle that is still being
  detected never absorbs another track, so two cars driving close together stay two vehicles.
- A vehicle that has been saved keeps absorbing its own ID switches, so it is never saved a second time.

### The buffer: keep the best frame, drop the older ones

While a vehicle is inside an ROI its frames are **not saved**. Only the best candidate is held in memory
(score = confidence x size x how much of it is inside the ROI, penalised if cut by the frame edge); when a
better frame arrives it **replaces** the buffered one and the old frame is dropped. The vehicle is saved **once**:

| When | Why |
|---|---|
| it leaves the ROI | the normal case |
| it has not been seen for the duplicate window | it is gone for good |
| it has stayed `MAX_HOLD_SECONDS` in the ROI | stopped vehicles / traffic jams |
| you stop capture or restart for new settings | nothing buffered is lost (flush) |

`First frame (instant)` mode skips the buffer and saves the first good frame (the vehicle is still remembered, so
ID switches do not duplicate it).

The next car in the same lane is captured normally: a different car arriving later, or entering behind the
previous one, is not mistaken for it. File names never collide (`_2`, `_3` suffix).

## Files and folders

```
Data_capture_tool/
  backend/            Flask API, capture engine, dedup, storage, settings, devices, tests/
  frontend/           index.html + static/ (css, js, img, vendor/fontawesome)
  config.ini          settings (edited in place by the UI; comments are preserved)
  data/               cameras.json (RTSP URLs - git-ignored), thumbs/ (thumbnail cache)
  captures/           <camera>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/frame|crop/<camera>_<class>_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS_mmm>.jpg
  docs/               ARCHITECTURE.md, API.md
  AGENTS.md, llms.txt, llms-full.txt     for AI assistants
```

With **Keep metadata** on, each image gets a same-named `.json`:
`{camera, class, conf, track_id, bbox, timestamp, model, save_mode}`.

## config.ini

Edit the file or use the Settings tab (the UI edits lines in place, so your comments survive).

| Section | Key | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| App | `DEBUG` | `true` | DEBUG logging + Flask debug mode (reloader off). The interactive debugger is **never** enabled when the server is reachable from the network. |
| App | `HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | `0.0.0.0` = reachable from other machines; `127.0.0.1` = this machine only. |
| App | `PORT` | `5100` | Web UI port (1 - 65535). Edit it here and restart the service. |
| Paths | `MODELS_DIR` | `../models` | Relative to `config.ini`. `~` = the home folder of the user running the service (e.g. `~/_VIDES/_backend_service_combined/models`); environment variables are expanded; a path starting with `/` is taken from the filesystem root. |
| Paths | `OUTPUT_DIR` | `./captures` | |
| Model | `MODEL` | | file inside `MODELS_DIR` |
| Model | `DEVICE` | `auto` | `auto`, `cpu`, `cuda:0`, `cuda:0,cuda:1` |
| Model | `HALF` | `true` | FP16 on CUDA only |
| Model | `CONF_THRESH` | `0.25` | 0.01 - 1 |
| Model | `IMG_SIZE` | `640` | 160 - 2048 |
| Model | `CLASSES` | empty | class **names**, comma separated; empty = auto |
| Capture | `SAVE_MODE` | `frame` | `frame` / `crop` / `both` |
| Capture | `SAVE_METADATA` | `false` | |
| Capture | `WHEN` | `best` | `best` (buffer the best frame, save once) / `first` (save immediately) |
| Capture | `MIN_BOX` | `40` | 1 - 5000 |
| Capture | `MIN_ROI_OVERLAP` | `0.5` | 0 - 1 |
| Capture | `JPEG_QUALITY` | `95` | 1 - 100 |
| Capture | `PAD_NORMAL` / `PAD_BIKE` | `0.15` / `0.40` | crop padding |
| Capture | `DEDUP_SECONDS` | `2` | 0 - 120. Window for re-linking a lost vehicle after a tracker ID switch |
| Capture | `MAX_HOLD_SECONDS` | `10` | 1 - 600. Save a vehicle that stays inside the ROI this long |

Environment variables: `HOST` and `PORT` (override `config.ini`), `DCT_CONFIG` and `DCT_DATA` (use another
config file / data folder - handy for testing without touching your real setup).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| Other machines cannot open the page | Check `HOST = 0.0.0.0`, that you use the address printed at start, and that the OS firewall allows the `PORT` (Windows: inbound rule for TCP 5100). |
| No models in the dropdown | `MODELS_DIR` does not exist for the user running the service, or has no `*.pt` files. Settings > Model shows the resolved folder and whether it was found (`GET /api/paths`). |
| Snapshot / Test says `Cannot reach host:port (timed out)` | The camera is offline, the port is wrong, or it is blocked. The tool checks the TCP port first so this fails in ~4 s instead of hanging. |
| `did not respond with a picture` | Port is open but the stream path or credentials are wrong, or the camera is at its connection limit. |
| Card says `reconnecting` | The stream dropped; it retries with backoff. The message under the chip says why. |
| Start says "Draw an ROI" | The camera has no ROI yet - use the ROI tab. |
| Start says "Model file not found" | Pick an existing model in Settings. |
| Settings Save says a class was ignored | The class name is not in the selected model; it is reported, never silent. |
| One vehicle captured twice | Raise **Duplicate window** a little (e.g. 3-4 s) or use a faster model/device so the tracker keeps up; check `Best frame` mode is on. Two vehicles close together are deliberately kept separate. |
| Nothing is captured | Check the ROI covers the road, confidence is not too high, classes include the vehicle type, and min size/overlap are not too strict. |
| Stop takes a few seconds | The stream was hung; shutdown waits for the reader (max ~10 s). |

```bash
python -m pytest                          # ~100 s: unit + API + real-model integration (needs ../vedio and ../models)
python -m pytest --ignore=backend/tests/test_integration.py     # fast: ~10 s
python scripts/build_llms_full.py        # regenerate llms-full.txt after editing docs
```

Details for contributors and AI assistants: [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md),
[`docs/API.md`](docs/API.md), [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md).

# FILE: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

# Architecture

A single Flask process serves a static frontend and a JSON API. Capture work runs in per-camera worker threads
inside that process. There is no database: state is JSON files, image files and `config.ini`.

```
Browser (frontend/)  <--HTTP/JSON, MJPEG-->  Flask app (backend/app.py)
                                               |-- CameraStore  -> data/cameras.json
                                               |-- settings     -> config.ini (edited in place)
                                               |-- storage      -> captures/**.jpg (+ .json), data/thumbs/
                                               '-- CameraWorker (one per running camera)
                                                     |-- LatestFrameReader thread  (RTSP -> newest frame)
                                                     |-- detect loop: YoloDetector + CaptureLogic
                                                     '-- saver thread (queue -> disk)
```

## Backend modules (`backend/`)

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `app.py` | `create_app(...)` builds the Flask app: REST API, MJPEG stream, restart-on-settings-change, status merging. `main()` runs it. Dependency-injected (`worker_factory`, `names_loader`, `device_detector`, `grabber`) so tests need no camera or GPU. |
| `capture_logic.py` | `CaptureLogic` + `Detection`: vehicle identity (links tracker-ID switches by motion prediction, drops double boxes), the best-frame **buffer**, when to save. Pure and unit-tested (no threads/model/camera). |
| `capture_engine.py` | `YoloDetector` (YOLO + ByteTrack via `trackers/bytetrack_vehicle.yaml`, class-agnostic NMS), `LatestFrameReader`, `CameraWorker` (threads, reconnect, preview JPEG), `default_classes`, `load_model_names`. |
| `dedup.py` | `iou`, `same_object` (one object boxed twice), `phash`. |
| `roi.py` | Polygon helpers: `point_in_polygon`, `box_overlap_ratio` (cached mask), `make_mask`, `expand_bbox`, `polygon_bbox`, `as_polygons`. Accept one polygon or a list. |
| `storage.py` | `CameraStore` (atomic JSON, migrates old single `roi` -> `rois`), `save_capture`, `list_captures`, `recent_captures`, `make_thumbnail`, `safe_capture_path`, `delete_capture`, `mask_url`. |
| `settings.py` | `load` / `save` for `config.ini`: typed values, defaults, choice + range validation, line-preserving writes. |
| `devices.py` | `detect` (cached GPU probe), `resolve` (parse `DEVICE`, fall back with warnings), `assign` (round-robin cameras over devices). |
| `camera_io.py` | `CameraError`, `check_port`, `run_with_timeout`, `open_capture` (5 s open/read timeouts), `grab_frame`. |

## Capture logic (`capture_logic.CaptureLogic.process`)

State: `_vehicles` (vid -> `_Vehicle`: last box/centre/size, smoothed velocity, `last_seen`, the buffered `best`
candidate, `saved`) and `_by_track` (tracker id -> vid).

For every frame:
1. `_suppress_overlaps`: detections of the same object (`dedup.same_object`: IoU > 0.5, or the smaller box mostly
   inside the larger and not tiny next to it) keep only the most confident one.
2. Detections whose tracker id is known go to their vehicle. A detection with an **unknown** id is matched to a
   vehicle that is **not detected in this frame** and was seen within `DEDUP_SECONDS`
   (`_find_lost_vehicle`): with two or more sightings the expected spot is last position + velocity x dt
   (tolerance `size x (1 + 1.5 dt)`, or it simply stopped); with one sighting the tolerance is `size x (1 + 3 dt)`.
   No match -> a new vehicle. Linked ids increment `merged` (shown as "skipped" in the UI).
3. For each vehicle: `_assess` -> eligible (class, conf, min size, centre inside an ROI, overlap with the ROI mask)
   / still inside. Eligible frames update the buffer when their `_score` beats the buffered one (the older frame
   is dropped). In `WHEN=first` the first eligible frame is saved at once.
4. `_finalize` (save once, release the buffer) when: the vehicle's centre leaves the ROIs, it is unseen for longer
   than `DEDUP_SECONDS`, it has been eligible for `MAX_HOLD_SECONDS`, or `flush()` (stop / restart).
5. Saved vehicles are kept (to absorb their own ID switches) and forgotten `DEDUP_SECONDS + 5 s` after last seen.

Requests returned: `{track_id, vehicle_id, cls, conf, box, frame, ts}`; the saver thread writes them.

## Restart-on-save (`app.py`)

`PUT /api/settings` saves, compares old vs new for the worker-relevant keys, and if any changed calls
`restart_running()`: every running camera is marked in `restarting`, then a thread stops the old worker and
`start_worker` builds a new one. `start_worker` adds the old worker's counters to `carry[cid]` under the lock, so
`/api/capture/status` shows continuous counters; state reads `restarting` meanwhile. The MJPEG stream re-reads
`workers[cid]` each loop so the browser connection survives the swap. A failed restart is reported through `failed[cid]`.

## Frontend (`frontend/`)

Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no framework. `index.html` + `static/js/{app,live,roi,cameras,gallery,settings}.js`.
The Live tab toolbar (`live.js`) calls `/api/capture/start-all` and `/api/capture/stop-all` and stores the chosen cameras-per-row layout in `localStorage` (`liveCols`). `app.js` holds helpers (`h()` DOM builder, `api()`, `toast`, `showTab`, shared lightbox, `debounce`, `timeAgo`).
Each tab registers `tabs.<name>.onShow`. All DOM is built with `h()`/`textContent` (no `innerHTML`). Font Awesome
is vendored in `static/vendor/fontawesome`. Settings uses a *draft* object and sends it once on Save & restart.
Deep links: `/#settings`, `/#live`, ...

## Data formats

`data/cameras.json`:
```json
[{"id": "ab12cd34", "name": "Cam-01", "url": "rtsp://user:pass@host:554/s", "enabled": true,
  "rois": [[[x, y], [x, y], [x, y]]], "frame_size": [1920, 1080], "device": null}]
```
(`rois` = list of polygons, each >= 3 points in true frame pixels. The API never returns the real password.)

Capture file: `captures/<camera>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<frame|crop>/<camera>_<class>_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS_mmm>[_N].jpg`.
Class names may contain underscores (`auto_rickshaw`); the camera comes from the folder name.

## Threading and safety notes

- `wlock` guards the `workers` dict; `CameraStore` has an `RLock` and writes via temp file + `os.replace`.
- `CameraWorker.stop()` sets the stop event, joins threads (<= 10 s each) and only then reports `stopped`.
- A worker exception sets state `error`, sets the stop event (so the saver exits) and `start` replaces it.
- Path traversal: all capture/thumbnail paths go through `storage.safe_capture_path` (rejects `..`, backslashes,
  absolute and drive paths; only `.jpg`).
- The service binds `HOST` (default `0.0.0.0`) on `PORT` from `config.ini` and has no authentication: run it on a trusted network.
  `app.server_options()` keeps Flask's interactive debugger off whenever the host is not loopback (DEBUG logging stays on); the reloader is always off.
  No browser is opened at start; the banner prints the local and LAN URLs.

# FILE: docs/API.md
==============================================================================

# HTTP API

Base URL `http://<host>:<PORT>` (default port 5100; the service listens on `0.0.0.0`, there is no authentication). JSON unless noted. Errors: `{"error": "message"}` with status 400/404/502.
Camera objects returned by the API have the RTSP password replaced by `****`.

## Cameras
| Method & path | Body / query | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/cameras` | | list of cameras `{id,name,url(masked),enabled,rois,frame_size,device}` |
| `POST /api/cameras` | `{name,url,device?}` | the new camera (400 if name/url empty) |
| `PUT /api/cameras/<id>` | any of `{name,url,enabled,device}` | camera. `enabled:false` stops its worker. A masked URL (`****`) is ignored. |
| `DELETE /api/cameras/<id>` | | `{ok}` (stops its worker; images are kept) |
| `POST /api/cameras/<id>/test` | | `{ok:true,size:[w,h]}` or `{ok:false,error}` (<= ~15 s) |
| `GET /api/cameras/<id>/snapshot` | | JPEG with header `X-Frame-Size: WxH`; 502 + reason if unreachable |
| `PUT /api/cameras/<id>/roi` | `{rois:[[[x,y],...],...], frame_size:[w,h]}` (legacy `{points}` = one ROI) | camera. Every polygon needs >= 3 points; `[]` clears. |

## Settings, models, devices
| Method & path | Notes |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/settings` | all `config.ini` values, typed |
| `PUT /api/settings` | partial update. Validates choices/ranges (400 on error). If any worker-relevant key actually changed, running cameras restart once (counters kept). `MODEL` must exist in `MODELS_DIR`. |
| `GET /api/models` | sorted `*.pt` names in `MODELS_DIR` |
| `GET /api/paths` | `{models_dir, models_dir_exists, models_count, output_dir}`: the resolved folders (`~`, env vars and relative paths expanded) |
| `GET /api/model/classes?model=` | `{names, selected, default, warnings}`; `selected` honours `CLASSES`, unknown names go to `warnings` |
| `GET /api/devices` | `{gpus:[{id,name,memory_mb}], pool, warnings}` |

## Capture control
| Method & path | Notes |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/capture/<id>/start` | 400 if no ROI / model missing / model unloadable. `{ok,device,warnings}`; `{ok,already_running}` if running. Replaces a worker in `error`. |
| `POST /api/capture/<id>/stop` | `{ok}` |
| `POST /api/capture/start-all` | Starts every **enabled** camera. `{started, failed, skipped, already_running, results:{<id>:{name, ok\|error\|skipped\|already_running}}}`. A camera that cannot start (no ROI, model missing) is reported, never fatal. |
| `POST /api/capture/stop-all` | Stops all running cameras in parallel. `{stopped: n}` |
| `GET /api/capture/status` | `{<id>: {state, message, saved, skipped, device}}`. `state`: `connected`, `reconnecting`, `restarting`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `error`. Counters include previous workers of the same camera. |
| `GET /api/stream/<id>` | MJPEG (`multipart/x-mixed-replace`) live preview with ROI + boxes; 404 if never started; survives restarts |

## Captured images
| Method & path | Notes |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/captures?camera=&date=&class=&page=&per_page=` | `{total,page,per_page,items:[{path,camera,date,kind,class,name,ts}]}`, newest first (`per_page` <= 200) |
| `GET /api/captures/<path>` | the JPEG. `path` is `items[].path`. |
| `DELETE /api/captures/<path>` | deletes the image and its `.json` |
| `GET /api/recent?limit=10` | `{items:[...]}` newest across cameras, one per vehicle (crop preferred); default and UI use the latest 10 (max 100). Fast (reads newest date folders only). |
| `GET /api/thumb/<path>?w=320` | cached JPEG thumbnail (`w` 32 - 1280), `Cache-Control: max-age=3600` |

`ts` is local time `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. Invalid / escaping paths return 400 or 404.

# FILE: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md - guide for AI coding assistants

Data Capture Tool: a Flask + plain-JS app that captures one training image per vehicle from RTSP streams inside
user-drawn ROIs. Read `README.md` (usage), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (design) and `docs/API.md` (endpoints) first.
A compact index is in `llms.txt`; the whole documentation in one file is `llms-full.txt`.

## Layout
- `backend/` Python: `app.py` (API), `capture_engine.py` (workers, detector), `capture_logic.py` (vehicle identity + buffer), `dedup.py`, `roi.py`,
  `storage.py`, `settings.py`, `devices.py`, `camera_io.py`, `tests/`.
- `frontend/` static UI: `index.html`, `static/js/*.js`, `static/css/app.css`, `static/vendor/fontawesome/`.
- `config.ini` (settings), `data/` (cameras.json, thumbs/), `captures/` (output). `data/`, `captures/`, models are git-ignored.

## Run and test
```bash
python backend/app.py                                  # HOST/PORT from config.ini [App] (env HOST, PORT override; DCT_CONFIG, DCT_DATA)
python -m pytest --ignore=backend/tests/test_integration.py     # fast suite (~10 s)
python -m pytest                                       # + real-model integration (~100 s; needs ../vedio and ../models)
python scripts/build_llms_full.py                      # regenerate llms-full.txt after editing README/docs/AGENTS
```
Use `DCT_CONFIG` / `DCT_DATA` to run against a throw-away config and data folder; never test against the user's
real `config.ini` or `data/cameras.json` (it holds a real camera URL with a password).

## Conventions that matter
- **TDD**: write the failing test first (`backend/tests/`), watch it fail, then implement. `CaptureLogic`,
  `Deduper`, `storage`, `settings`, `devices` are pure and unit-tested; the API is tested with a fake worker
  (`worker_factory`) so no camera/GPU is needed. Keep that dependency injection.
- **No database.** State = `data/cameras.json` (atomic write), `config.ini`, image files. Do not add a DB.
- **`settings.save` edits lines in place** (comments survive). Add new keys to `DEFAULTS` (+ `CHOICES`/`RANGES`)
  and to `WORKER_KEYS` in `app.py` if a running worker must restart when it changes.
- **ROI data model** is `rois` (list of polygons). `roi.py` functions accept one polygon or a list.
- **Never expose camera passwords**: API responses go through `public()` / `storage.mask_url`.
- **Paths from clients** must go through `storage.safe_capture_path`. **Configured folders** (`MODELS_DIR`, `OUTPUT_DIR`) go through
  `settings.resolve_path` (`~`, env vars, relative-to-config, absolute) - never `base / value` directly.
- **Frontend**: no framework, no build step, no `innerHTML`; build DOM with `h()`. Settings edits are a *draft*
  applied only by "Save & restart". Icons are Font Awesome (vendored). Colours come only from the CSS variables at the top of `static/css/app.css` (dark default = VIDES palette, light via `[data-theme=light]`); never hard-code UI colours in JS/HTML (the ROI polygon colours in `roi.js` are intentional annotation colours). The page has no JS test runner here;
  UI changes were verified by driving headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol.
- **Capture logic** (`capture_logic.py`) is per *vehicle*, not per tracker id: it links ID switches by motion prediction, buffers
  the best frame and saves once. A vehicle that is still detected must never absorb a new track (two close cars stay two),
  and a different car arriving later must not be absorbed (it would be lost). Both have regression tests - keep them.
- **Network exposure**: the service binds `0.0.0.0` by default and has no login. `server_options()` must keep the Werkzeug
  interactive debugger OFF unless the host is loopback (it is remote code execution). It never opens a browser.
- Windows is the primary platform: use `pathlib`, avoid shell-specific code, `taskkill` not `kill`.

## Gotchas
- Worker states: `connected`, `reconnecting`, `restarting`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `error`. `error` workers are
  replaced on Start. `restarting` is synthesised in `/api/capture/status` while a settings restart is in flight.
- On Windows a second server can bind a port that an older one still holds - kill stale test servers
  (find them by `PORT`/`DCT_CONFIG` env) before re-testing.
- `cv2.VideoCapture` on an unreachable host hangs ~30 s: always go through `camera_io` (port check + timeouts).
- COCO models are recognised by class names (`person` + the four vehicle classes); anything else is "custom".
- Saved image names: `<cam>_<class>_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS_mmm>[_N].jpg`; class names can contain underscores.

## Do not
- Commit `config.ini` secrets, `data/`, `captures/`, `*.pt`. Do not start capture automatically.
- Add noisy dependencies; keep `requirements.txt` small.
